correctness.summary: The proof splits on whether the duplicated special columns meet at most one target class or at least two. Projection and padding invoke the original SHF in the first case; choosing any two special-bearing classes reduces the required ordinary sizes by one each, so a pair-residual auxiliary separates the second case. Zero residual parts, multiple special-bearing classes, repeated specials within one class, and the m-symbol budget were checked explicitly.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Zaverucha's 2010 thesis gives the two-class reduced one-column recurrence, an arbitrary-type one-column recurrence with unreduced auxiliary, the known Martirosyan--van Trung perfect-hash columns-increase recurrence, and an arbitrary-type multi-column recurrence with full-type auxiliary, while explicitly identifying room for improvement. Searches through later SHF, DHF, PHF, and frameproof-code literature found no pair-residual arbitrary-type recurrence or arbitrary-x reduced two-class specialization.

value.summary: The theorem supplies an arbitrary-type auxiliary whose constituent residual types all have total strength W-2, unifying the known perfect-hash and two-class reductions. It extends the reduced two-class mechanism to arbitrary admissible duplication width and gives explicit small-row specializations, including a logarithmic auxiliary for type {1,1,2}.

limitations: The pair-residual requirement is weaker in separation strength but is not guaranteed to use fewer rows than a full-type auxiliary in every parameter regime.
A vertical stack of residual-type ingredients can be nonoptimal because one array may satisfy several residual types simultaneously.
The frameproof lifting is elementary once the construction is recognized and is not asserted as an independently novel proof.
Originality retains residual risk from differently named, unindexed, or inaccessible work.
